MScFE 622 Stochastic Modeling - Group Work Project 1¶

Team: Inez Andriana Regita Cahyani, Lakshya Agarwal, Ssekyewa Richard

This notebook contains all the code for the project, in the order of the tasks:

Step Task Content
1a Member A Heston (1993) calibration to 15-day options via Lewis (2001)
1b Member B Heston (1993) calibration to 15-day options via Carr-Madan (1999), comparison with 1a
1c Member C Monte Carlo price of a 20-day ATM Asian call, plus the 4% fee
2a Member C Bates (1996) calibration to 60-day options via Lewis (2001)
2b Member A Bates (1996) calibration to 60-day options via Carr-Madan (1999), comparison with 2a
2c Member B Price of a 70-day put with 95% moneyness
3a Team Euribor term structure, cubic-spline interpolation, CIR (1985) calibration
3b Team 100,000 Monte Carlo simulations of the 12-month Euribor one year ahead

Common inputs: $S_0 = 232.90$ USD, constant risk-free rate $r = 1.50\%$, 250 trading days per year. The notebook runs top to bottom (Kernel > Restart & Run All); the full run takes a few minutes because of the brute-force grid searches.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared tools: Black-Scholes implied volatility, put-call parity check,
# generic MSE error function, fit statistics and plots.
# Every pricer below has the signature  pricer(S0, K, T, r, *params).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def BSM_value(S0, K, T, r, sigma, option_type):
    """Black-Scholes-Merton value of a European call ('C') or put ('P')."""
    d1 = (np.log(S0 / K) + (r + 0.5 * sigma**2) * T) / (sigma * np.sqrt(T))
    d2 = d1 - sigma * np.sqrt(T)
    call = S0 * norm.cdf(d1) - K * np.exp(-r * T) * norm.cdf(d2)
    return call if option_type == "C" else call - S0 + K * np.exp(-r * T)


def BSM_implied_vol(price, S0, K, T, r, option_type):
    """Black-Scholes implied volatility by root search (NaN if no root)."""
    try:
        return brentq(lambda s: BSM_value(S0, K, T, r, s, option_type) - price, 1e-4, 5.0)
    except ValueError:
        return np.nan


def put_from_call(call_fn):
    """Put pricer obtained from a call pricer via put-call parity."""
    def put_fn(S0, K, T, r, *params):
        return call_fn(S0, K, T, r, *params) - S0 + K * np.exp(-r * T)
    return put_fn


def parity_check(options):
    """Put-call parity and static no-arbitrage checks on the market quotes."""
    T = options["T"].iloc[0]
    calls = options[options["Type"] == "C"].set_index("Strike")["Price"]
    puts = options[options["Type"] == "P"].set_index("Strike")["Price"]
    parity = pd.DataFrame({"Call": calls, "Put": puts})
    parity["Market C - P"] = parity["Call"] - parity["Put"]
    parity["S0 - K exp(-rT)"] = S0 - parity.index * np.exp(-r * T)
    parity["Deviation"] = parity["Market C - P"] - parity["S0 - K exp(-rT)"]
    print("Put-call parity check on market quotes (T = %.4f years):" % T)
    display(parity.round(3))
    max_dev = parity["Deviation"].abs().max()
    if max_dev > 0.5:
        print("NOTE: parity deviations of up to %.2f USD. No arbitrage-free model can match calls"
              " and puts simultaneously; an MSE fit will split the difference." % max_dev)
    if (np.diff(calls.values) > 0).any():
        print("NOTE: call prices are not decreasing in strike (violation at K = %s)."
              % list(calls.index[1:][np.diff(calls.values) > 0]))
    if (np.diff(puts.values) < 0).any():
        print("NOTE: put prices are not increasing in strike (violation at K = %s)."
              % list(puts.index[1:][np.diff(puts.values) < 0]))
    # Theoretical MSE floor: the best any parity-consistent model can do is to put
    # the model call half-way between the market call and the parity-implied call.
    floor = np.mean((parity["Deviation"].values / 2) ** 2)
    print("Lowest MSE attainable by any parity-consistent model on these quotes: %.4f" % floor)
    return parity


PENALTY = 5000.0  # returned for infeasible parameters (far above any feasible MSE)


def make_error_function(options, call_fn, put_fn, check, log_every=200):
    """MSE between model and market prices over all rows of `options`.

    check(p) returns False for infeasible parameters, which are penalised.
    Prints a progress line every `log_every` evaluations.
    """
    types = options["Type"].values
    Ks = options["Strike"].values.astype(float)
    Ts = options["T"].values.astype(float)
    mkt = options["Price"].values.astype(float)
    state = {"i": 0, "min": PENALTY}

    def error(p):
        if not check(p):
            return PENALTY
        se = 0.0
        for typ, K, T, price in zip(types, Ks, Ts, mkt):
            fn = call_fn if typ == "C" else put_fn
            se += (fn(S0, K, T, r, *p) - price) ** 2
        mse = se / len(mkt)
        state["min"] = min(state["min"], mse)
        if state["i"] % log_every == 0:
            print("%5d |" % state["i"],
                  np.array2string(np.asarray(p, float), precision=4, suppress_small=True),
                  "| %8.4f | %8.4f" % (mse, state["min"]))
        state["i"] += 1
        return mse

    return error


def fit_table(options, call_fn, put_fn, params):
    """Market vs model prices, pricing errors and implied volatilities."""
    df = options[["Type", "Strike", "Price", "T"]].copy()
    df["Model"] = [(call_fn if t == "C" else put_fn)(S0, K, T, r, *params)
                   for t, K, T in zip(df["Type"], df["Strike"], df["T"])]
    df["Error"] = df["Model"] - df["Price"]
    df["Market IV"] = [BSM_implied_vol(p, S0, K, T, r, t)
                       for p, K, T, t in zip(df["Price"], df["Strike"], df["T"], df["Type"])]
    df["Model IV"] = [BSM_implied_vol(p, S0, K, T, r, t)
                      for p, K, T, t in zip(df["Model"], df["Strike"], df["T"], df["Type"])]
    mse = np.mean(df["Error"] ** 2)
    print("MSE  = %.4f" % mse)
    print("RMSE = %.4f USD" % np.sqrt(mse))
    print("Mean absolute error = %.4f USD" % df["Error"].abs().mean())
    print("Max  absolute error = %.4f USD" % df["Error"].abs().max())
    return df.drop(columns="T"), mse


def plot_fit(fit, call_fn, put_fn, params, days, model_label, title, filename):
    """2x2 figure: call prices, put prices, pricing errors, implied-vol smile."""
    T = days / DAYS
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 9))
    K_grid = np.linspace(225, 240, 61)
    call_curve = [call_fn(S0, K, T, r, *params) for K in K_grid]
    put_curve = [put_fn(S0, K, T, r, *params) for K in K_grid]
    for ax, typ, curve, name in [(axes[0, 0], "C", call_curve, "Call"),
                                 (axes[0, 1], "P", put_curve, "Put")]:
        sub = fit[fit["Type"] == typ]
        ax.plot(sub["Strike"], sub["Price"], "o", ms=8, label="Market price")
        ax.plot(K_grid, curve, "-", lw=2, label=model_label)
        ax.axvline(S0, color="grey", ls=":", lw=1, label="Spot $S_0$ = %.2f" % S0)
        ax.set_title("%s prices, T = %d days" % (name, days))
        ax.set_xlabel("Strike K (USD)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Option price (USD)")
        ax.legend()
    ax = axes[1, 0]
    width = 0.9
    for typ, offset, name in [("C", -width / 2, "Calls"), ("P", width / 2, "Puts")]:
        sub = fit[fit["Type"] == typ]
        ax.bar(sub["Strike"] + offset, sub["Error"], width=width, label=name)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_title("Pricing errors (model - market)")
    ax.set_xlabel("Strike K (USD)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Error (USD)")
    ax.legend()
    ax = axes[1, 1]
    for typ, marker, name in [("C", "o", "Call"), ("P", "s", "Put")]:
        sub = fit[fit["Type"] == typ]
        ax.plot(sub["Strike"], 100 * sub["Market IV"], marker, ms=8, label="Market %s IV" % name)
        ax.plot(sub["Strike"], 100 * sub["Model IV"], marker + "--", mfc="none", ms=8,
                label="Model %s IV" % name)
    ax.axvline(S0, color="grey", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.set_title("Black-Scholes implied volatility, T = %d days" % days)
    ax.set_xlabel("Strike K (USD)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Implied volatility (%)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=14)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG_DIR, filename), dpi=150)
    plt.show()

Step 1¶

Step 1 a) Heston (1993) calibration via Lewis (2001) - 15-day options (Member A)¶

Model. Under the risk-neutral measure the Heston (1993) model is

$$dS_t = r S_t\,dt + \sqrt{v_t}\,S_t\,dW_t^S,\qquad dv_t = \kappa_v(\theta_v - v_t)\,dt + \sigma_v\sqrt{v_t}\,dW_t^v,\qquad dW_t^S dW_t^v = \rho\,dt .$$

Pricing. The Lewis (2001) formula gives the European call as a single real integral of the characteristic function $\varphi$ of $\log(S_T/S_0)$:

$$C_0 = S_0 - \frac{\sqrt{S_0 K}\,e^{-rT}}{\pi}\int_0^\infty \mathrm{Re}\!\left[e^{iu\log(S_0/K)}\,\varphi\!\left(u - \tfrac{i}{2}\right)\right]\frac{du}{u^2 + 1/4}.$$

Puts are priced from the call by put-call parity $P = C - S_0 + K e^{-rT}$ (the preferred option in the brief).

Calibration. Target maturity 15 days ($T = 15/250 = 0.06$), all five calls and five puts. Error function: regular MSE in price. Optimisation: brute-force grid search over $(\kappa_v, \theta_v, \sigma_v, \rho, v_0)$ followed by a local Nelder-Mead refinement, with the Feller condition $2\kappa_v\theta_v \ge \sigma_v^2$ imposed. A second run without the Feller condition is a robustness check.

1 a) i. Heston (1993) characteristic function¶

In [3]:
def H93_char_func(u, T, r, kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0):
    """Heston (1993) characteristic function of log(S_T / S0)
    (Albrecher et al. 2007 'little trap' form, as in Hilpisch 2015)."""
    c1 = kappa_v * theta_v
    c2 = -np.sqrt((rho * sigma_v * u * 1j - kappa_v) ** 2 - sigma_v**2 * (-u * 1j - u**2))
    c3 = (kappa_v - rho * sigma_v * u * 1j + c2) / (kappa_v - rho * sigma_v * u * 1j - c2)
    H1 = r * u * 1j * T + (c1 / sigma_v**2) * (
        (kappa_v - rho * sigma_v * u * 1j + c2) * T
        - 2 * np.log((1 - c3 * np.exp(c2 * T)) / (1 - c3)))
    H2 = ((kappa_v - rho * sigma_v * u * 1j + c2) / sigma_v**2
          * ((1 - np.exp(c2 * T)) / (1 - c3 * np.exp(c2 * T))))
    return np.exp(H1 + H2 * v0)

1 a) ii. Lewis (2001) call pricer and put-call parity¶

In [4]:
def lewis_call_value(char_func, S0, K, T, r, params):
    """European call via the Lewis (2001) integral for any characteristic function."""
    def int_func(u):
        cf = char_func(u - 0.5j, T, r, *params)
        return 1 / (u**2 + 0.25) * (np.exp(1j * u * np.log(S0 / K)) * cf).real
    int_value = quad(int_func, 0, np.inf, limit=250)[0]
    return max(0.0, S0 - np.exp(-r * T) * np.sqrt(S0 * K) / np.pi * int_value)


def H93_call_value(S0, K, T, r, *params):
    """European call in Heston (1993) via Lewis (2001)."""
    return lewis_call_value(H93_char_func, S0, K, T, r, params)


H93_put_value = put_from_call(H93_call_value)

1 a) iii. Calibration set-up: parameter grid, feasibility (Feller) and optimiser¶

In [5]:
HESTON_NAMES = ["kappa_v", "theta_v", "sigma_v", "rho", "v0"]
HESTON_GRID = (
    (0.5, 10.6, 2.5),     # kappa_v
    (0.05, 0.31, 0.05),   # theta_v
    (0.1, 1.01, 0.3),     # sigma_v
    (-0.9, 0.51, 0.35),   # rho
    (0.05, 0.21, 0.05),   # v0
)


def heston_ok(p, feller=True):
    """Feasibility of a Heston parameter vector."""
    kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0 = p
    if kappa_v < 0.0 or theta_v < 0.005 or sigma_v < 0.0 or rho < -1.0 or rho > 1.0 or v0 < 0.0:
        return False
    if feller and 2 * kappa_v * theta_v < sigma_v**2:
        return False
    return True


def calibrate_heston(options, call_fn, put_fn, feller=True, log_every=200):
    """Brute-force grid search followed by Nelder-Mead on the MSE error function."""
    error = make_error_function(options, call_fn, put_fn, lambda p: heston_ok(p, feller), log_every)
    print("    i | (kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0) |   MSE    | min MSE")
    p0 = brute(error, HESTON_GRID, finish=None)
    print("Brute-force result:", np.round(p0, 4))
    opt = fmin(error, p0, xtol=1e-6, ftol=1e-6, maxiter=1500, maxfun=2000)
    return opt, error(opt)


def print_heston_params(opt, mse):
    for name, value in zip(HESTON_NAMES, opt):
        print("%-8s = %9.4f" % (name, value))
    print("Implied initial volatility  sqrt(v0)      = %.2f%%" % (100 * np.sqrt(opt[4])))
    print("Implied long-run volatility sqrt(theta_v) = %.2f%%" % (100 * np.sqrt(opt[1])))
    print("Feller condition 2*kappa*theta - sigma^2  = %.5f" % (2 * opt[0] * opt[1] - opt[2] ** 2))
    print("MSE = %.4f, RMSE = %.4f USD" % (mse, np.sqrt(mse)))

Step 1 b) Heston (1993) calibration via Carr-Madan (1999) - 15-day options (Member B)¶

Same model, same data, same error function and same optimiser as Step 1 a), but the call price is computed with the Carr-Madan (1999) FFT instead of the Lewis integral. The damped call price $c(k) = e^{\alpha k} C(k)$, $k = \log(K/S_0)$, has Fourier transform

$$\psi(v) = \frac{e^{-rT}\,\varphi\!\big(v - (\alpha + 1)i\big)}{\alpha^2 + \alpha - v^2 + i(2\alpha + 1)v},$$

and the call is recovered by one FFT over $N = 4096$ log-strikes with Simpson weights, $\alpha = 1.5$. The grid is shifted so that the target strike falls exactly on a grid node (no interpolation). Puts again come from put-call parity.

Because both methods evaluate the same characteristic function, they must give the same prices for the same parameters; the first cell below verifies this numerically. Any difference between the Step 1 a) and 1 b) parameters therefore comes from the optimiser, not from the pricing method.

In [11]:
def CM_call_value(char_func, S0, K, T, r, params, N=4096, eps=1.0 / 150, alpha=1.5):
    """European call via the Carr-Madan (1999) FFT for any characteristic function of log(S_T/S0).

    Prices are computed for unit spot and scaled by S0 (homogeneity). The log-strike grid has
    spacing eps and is shifted by b = N eps / 2 - k so that k = log(K/S0) sits on node N/2.
    """
    k = np.log(K / S0)
    eta = 2 * np.pi / (N * eps)
    b = 0.5 * N * eps - k
    u = np.arange(1, N + 1)
    vo = eta * (u - 1)
    v = vo - (alpha + 1) * 1j
    mod_char_func = (np.exp(-r * T) * char_func(v, T, r, *params)
                     / (alpha**2 + alpha - vo**2 + 1j * (2 * alpha + 1) * vo))
    delt = np.zeros(N)
    delt[0] = 1
    j = np.arange(1, N + 1)
    simpson_w = (3 + (-1) ** j - delt) / 3
    fft_func = np.exp(1j * b * vo) * mod_char_func * eta * simpson_w
    payoff = np.fft.fft(fft_func).real
    call_values = np.exp(-alpha * k) / np.pi * payoff
    pos = int(round((k + b) / eps))
    return max(0.0, call_values[pos] * S0)


def H93_call_value_CM(S0, K, T, r, *params):
    """European call in Heston (1993) via Carr-Madan (1999)."""
    return CM_call_value(H93_char_func, S0, K, T, r, params)


H93_put_value_CM = put_from_call(H93_call_value_CM)

def bounded_ok(p):

Step 1 c) Pricing the 20-day ATM Asian call by Monte Carlo (Member C)¶

Contract. Arithmetic-average Asian call, at the money ($K = S_0 = 232.90$), 20 trading days, payoff $\max(\bar S - K, 0)$ with $\bar S = \frac{1}{21}\sum_{t=0}^{20} S_t$ (today's price $S_0$ is included).

Model and parameters. Heston (1993) with the Step 1 a) parameters (Lewis calibration, fitted to both calls and puts with the Feller condition, so the variance stays positive). They are the closest calibration to the contract's 20-day maturity.

Simulation. Full-truncation Euler scheme with one step per trading day ($\Delta t = 1/250$), 200,000 paths, risk-neutral drift $r$. The price is the discounted mean payoff; the standard error, a 95% confidence interval and a convergence plot show that the number of paths is sufficient.

Fee. The bank charges 4% on top of the fair price: client price $= 1.04 \times$ fair price.

In [16]:
def heston_paths(params, T, n_steps, n_paths, seed):
    """Full-truncation Euler simulation of Heston (1993) under the risk-neutral measure.

    Returns the price paths S (n_paths x (n_steps + 1)), including S0 in column 0.
    """
    kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0 = params
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    dt = T / n_steps
    S = np.empty((n_paths, n_steps + 1))
    S[:, 0] = S0
    v = np.full(n_paths, v0)
    for t in range(n_steps):
        z1 = rng.standard_normal(n_paths)
        z2 = rng.standard_normal(n_paths)
        zs = z1
        zv = rho * z1 + np.sqrt(1 - rho**2) * z2
        v_pos = np.maximum(v, 0.0)
        S[:, t + 1] = S[:, t] * np.exp((r - 0.5 * v_pos) * dt + np.sqrt(v_pos * dt) * zs)
        v = v + kappa_v * (theta_v - v_pos) * dt + sigma_v * np.sqrt(v_pos * dt) * zv
    return S


def asian_call_mc(params, K, days, n_paths, seed=2024):
    """Discounted arithmetic-average Asian call payoffs (one per path)."""
    T = days / DAYS
    S = heston_paths(params, T, days, n_paths, seed)
    average = S.mean(axis=1)                       # includes S0, days + 1 observations
    return np.exp(-r * T) * np.maximum(average - K, 0.0), S

Step 2¶

Step 2 a) Bates (1996) calibration via Lewis (2001) - 60-day options (Member C)¶

Model. Bates (1996) adds Merton (1976) log-normal jumps to Heston (1993):

$$\frac{dS_t}{S_{t^-}} = (r - \lambda\bar\mu)\,dt + \sqrt{v_t}\,dW_t^S + (e^{J} - 1)\,dN_t,\qquad J \sim N(\mu, \delta^2),\qquad \bar\mu = e^{\mu + \delta^2/2} - 1,$$

with $N_t$ a Poisson process of intensity $\lambda$ independent of the Brownian motions. Because the diffusion and jump parts are independent, the characteristic function of $\log(S_T/S_0)$ is the product of the Heston characteristic function and the (compensated) Merton jump characteristic function. The eight parameters are $(\kappa_v, \theta_v, \sigma_v, \rho, v_0, \lambda, \mu, \delta)$.

Pricing. Lewis (2001) integral, as in Step 1 a); puts by put-call parity.

Calibration steps for Bates (target maturity 60 days, $T = 0.24$, five calls and five puts, MSE):

  1. Calibrate the five Heston parameters with the jump component switched off ($\lambda = 0$): brute-force grid search then Nelder-Mead, Feller condition imposed.
  2. Holding the Heston parameters fixed, calibrate the three jump parameters $(\lambda, \mu, \delta)$: brute force then Nelder-Mead.
  3. Joint Nelder-Mead refinement of all eight parameters from the Stage 1 + 2 solution.
In [19]:
def M76J_char_func(u, T, lamb, mu, delta):
    """Characteristic function of the compensated Merton (1976) jump component."""
    omega = -lamb * (np.exp(mu + 0.5 * delta**2) - 1)  # martingale correction
    return np.exp((1j * u * omega + lamb * (np.exp(1j * u * mu - 0.5 * u**2 * delta**2) - 1)) * T)


def B96_char_func(u, T, r, kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0, lamb, mu, delta):
    """Bates (1996) characteristic function of log(S_T / S0)."""
    return H93_char_func(u, T, r, kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0) * M76J_char_func(u, T, lamb, mu, delta)


def B96_call_value(S0, K, T, r, *params):
    """European call in Bates (1996) via Lewis (2001)."""
    return lewis_call_value(B96_char_func, S0, K, T, r, params)


B96_put_value = put_from_call(B96_call_value)

BATES_NAMES = HESTON_NAMES + ["lamb", "mu", "delta"]
JUMP_GRID = (
    (0.0, 0.51, 0.1),    # lamb
    (-0.5, 0.21, 0.1),   # mu
    (0.0, 0.51, 0.1),    # delta
)


def bates_ok(p, feller=True):
    kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0, lamb, mu, delta = p
    if not heston_ok(p[:5], feller):
        return False
    if lamb < 0.0 or lamb > 10.0 or mu < -0.6 or mu > 0.6 or delta < 0.0:
        return False
    return True


def calibrate_bates(options, call_fn, put_fn, feller=True, log_every=200):
    """Three-stage calibration of Bates (1996): Heston only, jumps only, joint refinement."""
    error = make_error_function(options, call_fn, put_fn, lambda p: bates_ok(p, feller), log_every)
    no_jumps = np.zeros(3)

    print("\nStage 1: Heston (1993) parameters, jumps switched off (lambda = 0)")
    print("    i | (kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0, lamb, mu, delta) |   MSE    | min MSE")
    h93_error = lambda p5: error(np.concatenate([p5, no_jumps]))
    p_h93 = brute(h93_error, HESTON_GRID, finish=None)
    p_h93 = fmin(h93_error, p_h93, xtol=1e-6, ftol=1e-6, maxiter=1500, maxfun=2000)
    mse_h93 = h93_error(p_h93)
    print("Stage 1 result:", np.round(p_h93, 4), "MSE = %.4f" % mse_h93)

    print("\nStage 2: jump parameters (lambda, mu, delta), Heston parameters fixed")
    jump_error = lambda p3: error(np.concatenate([p_h93, p3]))
    p_jump = brute(jump_error, JUMP_GRID, finish=None)
    p_jump = fmin(jump_error, p_jump, xtol=1e-6, ftol=1e-6, maxiter=1000, maxfun=1500)
    mse_jump = jump_error(p_jump)
    print("Stage 2 result:", np.round(p_jump, 4), "MSE = %.4f" % mse_jump)

    print("\nStage 3: joint calibration of all eight parameters")
    p_full = np.concatenate([p_h93, p_jump])
    opt = fmin(error, p_full, xtol=1e-6, ftol=1e-6, maxiter=3000, maxfun=4000)
    mse_full = error(opt)
    print("Stage 3 result:", np.round(opt, 4), "MSE = %.4f" % mse_full)

    stages = pd.DataFrame({"Stage 1 (Heston)": np.concatenate([p_h93, no_jumps]),
                           "Stage 2 (+ jumps)": p_full, "Stage 3 (joint)": opt}, index=BATES_NAMES)
    stages.loc["MSE"] = [mse_h93, mse_jump, mse_full]
    return opt, mse_full, stages


def print_bates_params(opt, mse):
    for name, value in zip(BATES_NAMES, opt):
        print("%-8s = %9.4f" % (name, value))
    kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0, lamb, mu, delta = opt
    print("Implied initial volatility  sqrt(v0)      = %.2f%%" % (100 * np.sqrt(v0)))
    print("Implied long-run volatility sqrt(theta_v) = %.2f%%" % (100 * np.sqrt(theta_v)))
    print("Feller condition 2*kappa*theta - sigma^2  = %.5f" % (2 * kappa_v * theta_v - sigma_v**2))
    print("Expected jumps per year (lambda)          = %.4f" % lamb)
    print("Expected jump size E[exp(J) - 1]          = %.2f%%" % (100 * (np.exp(mu + 0.5 * delta**2) - 1)))
    print("MSE = %.4f, RMSE = %.4f USD" % (mse, np.sqrt(mse)))
    bounds = {"theta_v": (0.005, None), "rho": (-1.0, 1.0), "lamb": (0.0, 10.0),
              "mu": (-0.6, 0.6), "delta": (0.0, None), "sigma_v": (0.0, None)}
    at_bound = [n for n, val in zip(BATES_NAMES, opt) if n in bounds
                and any(b is not None and abs(val - b) < 1e-3 for b in bounds[n])]
    if at_bound:
        print("NOTE: parameters at a constraint boundary: %s (weakly identified by ten"
              " near-the-money quotes at one maturity)." % ", ".join(at_bound))

Step 2 b) Bates (1996) calibration via Carr-Madan (1999) - 60-day options (Member A)¶

Same model, data, error function and three-stage procedure as Step 2 a), with the Carr-Madan (1999) FFT pricer of Step 1 b) applied to the Bates characteristic function. The first cell verifies that Carr-Madan and Lewis agree at identical parameters, so that any parameter difference between 2 a) and 2 b) can be attributed to the optimisation (flat objective, parameters at bounds) rather than to the pricing method. A run without the Feller condition is a robustness check.

Step 2 c) Pricing a 70-day put with 95% moneyness (Member B)¶

Contract. European put on SM, 70 trading days ($T = 0.28$), strike $K = 0.95\,S_0 = 221.255$.

Parameters. The 60-day calibrations of Step 2 are the closest to a 70-day maturity, so the Step 2 b) Bates parameters (Carr-Madan, calls and puts) are the primary choice. The 15-day Heston parameters of Step 1 b) are shown as a comparison: they describe the very short end of the volatility surface and carry no information about 60 to 70-day options.

Method. As in Step 1 c), the fair price is obtained by risk-neutral Monte Carlo (200,000 paths, one step per trading day, full-truncation Euler, jumps simulated as a compound Poisson process) with a standard error and a convergence plot. The semi-closed-form Carr-Madan price (call, then put-call parity) is the benchmark that the simulation must reproduce. The 4% fee is then applied.

In [27]:
def bates_terminal_prices(params, T, n_steps, n_paths, seed):
    """Full-truncation Euler simulation of Bates (1996) terminal prices S_T under Q.

    Jumps: compound Poisson with intensity lamb, log-jump sizes N(mu, delta^2),
    drift compensated by -lamb * (exp(mu + delta^2 / 2) - 1).
    """
    kappa_v, theta_v, sigma_v, rho, v0, lamb, mu, delta = params
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    dt = T / n_steps
    comp = lamb * (np.exp(mu + 0.5 * delta**2) - 1)
    logS = np.full(n_paths, np.log(S0))
    v = np.full(n_paths, v0)
    for _ in range(n_steps):
        z1 = rng.standard_normal(n_paths)
        z2 = rng.standard_normal(n_paths)
        zs = z1
        zv = rho * z1 + np.sqrt(1 - rho**2) * z2
        v_pos = np.maximum(v, 0.0)
        n_jumps = rng.poisson(lamb * dt, n_paths) if lamb > 0 else np.zeros(n_paths, int)
        jump = np.where(n_jumps > 0,
                        mu * n_jumps + delta * np.sqrt(n_jumps) * rng.standard_normal(n_paths), 0.0)
        logS += (r - comp - 0.5 * v_pos) * dt + np.sqrt(v_pos * dt) * zs + jump
        v = v + kappa_v * (theta_v - v_pos) * dt + sigma_v * np.sqrt(v_pos * dt) * zv
    return np.exp(logS)

Step 3¶

Step 3 a) Euribor term structure, cubic-spline interpolation and CIR (1985) calibration¶

Term structure. Euribor fixings are simple money-market rates: a deposit of tenor $\tau$ at rate $L$ grows by $1 + L\tau$. Each fixing is converted to a continuously compounded zero rate $R(\tau) = \ln(1 + L\tau)/\tau$ and a discount factor $P(0,\tau) = e^{-R(\tau)\tau}$. Year fractions: 1 week $= 1/52$, 1 month $= 1/12$, 3 months $= 0.25$, 6 months $= 0.5$, 12 months $= 1$.

Interpolation. A cubic spline through the five zero rates is evaluated on a weekly grid $t_k = k/52$, $k = 1,\dots,52$. Simple-rate equivalents, instantaneous forwards $f(t) = R(t) + t R'(t)$ and discount factors are reported for the interpolated curve.

CIR model. $dr_t = \kappa(\theta - r_t)\,dt + \sigma\sqrt{r_t}\,dW_t$ with closed-form zero-coupon bond price $P(t, T) = A(\tau)e^{-B(\tau) r_t}$, $\tau = T - t$, hence model zero rate $R(\tau) = -\ln A(\tau)/\tau + B(\tau) r_0/\tau$. The four parameters $(r_0, \kappa, \theta, \sigma)$ are calibrated by minimising the MSE between model and interpolated zero rates over the 52 weekly points (multi-start Nelder-Mead, Feller condition $2\kappa\theta \ge \sigma^2$ imposed).

def cir_bond_price(tau, r_t, kappa, theta, sigma):
    """CIR (1985) zero-coupon bond price P(t, t + tau) = A exp(-B r_t)."""
    tau = np.asarray(tau, dtype=float)
    gamma = np.sqrt(kappa**2 + 2 * sigma**2)
    eg = np.exp(gamma * tau)
    denom = (gamma + kappa) * (eg - 1) + 2 * gamma
    B = 2 * (eg - 1) / denom
    A = (2 * gamma * np.exp((kappa + gamma) * tau / 2) / denom) ** (2 * kappa * theta / sigma**2)
    return A * np.exp(-B * r_t)


def cir_zero_rate(tau, r0, kappa, theta, sigma):
    """CIR continuously compounded zero rate for maturity tau."""
    tau = np.asarray(tau, dtype=float)
    return -np.log(cir_bond_price(tau, r0, kappa, theta, sigma)) / tau


def cir_mse(params, T, R_target):
    r0, kappa, theta, sigma = params
    if r0 <= 0 or kappa <= 0 or theta <= 0 or sigma <= 0:
        return 1e6
    if 2 * kappa * theta < sigma**2:              # Feller condition
        return 1e6
    model = cir_zero_rate(T, r0, kappa, theta, sigma)
    if np.any(~np.isfinite(model)):
        return 1e6
    return np.mean((model - R_target) ** 2)


def calibrate_cir(T, R_target, n_restarts=60, seed=7):
    """Multi-start Nelder-Mead minimisation of the MSE in zero rates."""
    bounds = [(0.001, 0.05), (0.01, 5.0), (0.001, 0.08), (0.001, 0.5)]   # r0, kappa, theta, sigma
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    best = None
    for _ in range(n_restarts):
        x0 = [rng.uniform(lo, hi) for lo, hi in bounds]
        res = minimize(cir_mse, x0, args=(T, R_target), method="Nelder-Mead",
                       options={"xatol": 1e-11, "fatol": 1e-13, "maxiter": 6000, "maxfev": 6000})
        if res.fun < 1e5 and (best is None or res.fun < best.fun):
            best = res
    return best

Step 3 b) Simulating the 12-month Euribor over the next year (100,000 Monte Carlo paths)¶

The calibrated CIR short rate is simulated daily for one year (250 steps) on 100,000 paths with the exact transition of the CIR process (a scaled non-central chi-square), which keeps rates positive without any truncation. On each simulated date $t$ the 12-month Euribor is read off the model: the CIR bond price $P(t, t+1) = A(1)e^{-B(1) r_t}$ gives the simple 12-month rate

$$L_{12m}(t) = \frac{1}{P(t, t+1)} - 1 .$$

From the distribution of $L_{12m}$ one year ahead we report (i) the range at a chosen confidence level, (ii) the expected value, and (iii) the implication for pricing products in one year versus today's 12-month Euribor of 2.556%.

In [32]:
N_PATHS_3B, N_STEPS_3B = 100_000, 250
dt_3b = 1.0 / N_STEPS_3B
rng = np.random.default_rng(2025)

# Exact CIR transition: r_{t+dt} = c * chi2_nc(df, nc), df = 4 kappa theta / sigma^2,
# c = sigma^2 (1 - e^{-kappa dt}) / (4 kappa), nc = r_t e^{-kappa dt} / c
df_3b = 4 * kappa_cir * theta_cir / sigma_cir**2
c_3b = sigma_cir**2 * (1 - np.exp(-kappa_cir * dt_3b)) / (4 * kappa_cir)
decay = np.exp(-kappa_cir * dt_3b)

A1 = cir_bond_price(1.0, 0.0, kappa_cir, theta_cir, sigma_cir)          # A(1)
B1 = -np.log(cir_bond_price(1.0, 1.0, kappa_cir, theta_cir, sigma_cir) / A1)  # B(1)
euribor_12m_from_r = lambda rt: 1.0 / (A1 * np.exp(-B1 * rt)) - 1.0   # simple 12-month rate

euribor_12m_today = 0.02556
model_12m_today = euribor_12m_from_r(r0_cir)

t0 = time.time()
r_t = np.full(N_PATHS_3B, r0_cir)
pct_levels = [0.5, 2.5, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95, 97.5, 99.5]
stats = {"day": [0], "mean_r": [r0_cir], "mean_L": [model_12m_today], "min_L": [model_12m_today],
         "max_L": [model_12m_today]}
for q in pct_levels:
    stats["p%g" % q] = [model_12m_today]
sample_paths = np.empty((50, N_STEPS_3B + 1))
sample_paths[:, 0] = model_12m_today
for step in range(1, N_STEPS_3B + 1):
    r_t = c_3b * rng.noncentral_chisquare(df_3b, r_t * decay / c_3b, N_PATHS_3B)
    L = euribor_12m_from_r(r_t)
    stats["day"].append(step)
    stats["mean_r"].append(r_t.mean())
    stats["mean_L"].append(L.mean())
    stats["min_L"].append(L.min())
    stats["max_L"].append(L.max())
    for q, val in zip(pct_levels, np.percentile(L, pct_levels)):
        stats["p%g" % q].append(val)
    sample_paths[:, step] = L[:50]
stats = pd.DataFrame(stats)
L_1y = L.copy()               # 12-month Euribor one year ahead, one value per path
r_1y = r_t.copy()
print("Simulated %d paths x %d daily steps in %.1f s" % (N_PATHS_3B, N_STEPS_3B, time.time() - t0))
print("Minimum short rate at the 1-year horizon over all paths: %.4f%% (positive, as the CIR model requires)"
      % (100 * r_1y.min()))

# (i) Range at the chosen confidence level, (ii) expected value, (iii) pricing implication
ci_levels = [(90, 5, 95), (95, 2.5, 97.5), (99, 0.5, 99.5)]
rows = []
for conf, lo, hi in ci_levels:
    rows.append({"Confidence level": "%d%%" % conf,
                 "Min 12m Euribor in 1y (%)": 100 * np.percentile(L_1y, lo),
                 "Max 12m Euribor in 1y (%)": 100 * np.percentile(L_1y, hi)})
range_table = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Confidence level")
display(range_table.round(3))

mean_1y = L_1y.mean()
se_mean_1y = L_1y.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(N_PATHS_3B)
# Analytical expectation of the CIR short rate for comparison
E_r_1y = theta_cir + (r0_cir - theta_cir) * np.exp(-kappa_cir * 1.0)
summary_3b = pd.Series({
    "Current 12m Euribor (market, %)": 100 * euribor_12m_today,
    "Current 12m Euribor (CIR model, %)": 100 * model_12m_today,
    "Expected 12m Euribor in 1 year (%)": 100 * mean_1y,
    "Std. error of the expectation (%)": 100 * se_mean_1y,
    "Median 12m Euribor in 1 year (%)": 100 * np.median(L_1y),
    "Std. deviation across paths (%)": 100 * L_1y.std(),
    "Absolute min over 100,000 paths (%)": 100 * L_1y.min(),
    "Absolute max over 100,000 paths (%)": 100 * L_1y.max(),
    "Expected short rate in 1 year, simulated (%)": 100 * r_1y.mean(),
    "Expected short rate in 1 year, analytical (%)": 100 * E_r_1y,
    "Prob. 12m Euribor in 1y above today's 2.556%": float((L_1y > euribor_12m_today).mean()),
})
display(summary_3b.round(4).to_frame("Value"))

shift_bps = 10000 * (mean_1y - euribor_12m_today)
print("Discount factor for a 1-year cash flow priced in one year: today %.5f vs expected %.5f in 1 year"
      % (1 / (1 + euribor_12m_today), 1 / (1 + mean_1y)))
print("Expected change in the 12m Euribor over the next year: %+.0f bps." % shift_bps)
print("A floating-rate liability indexed to 12m Euribor on a 10m notional would cost about %+.0f per year more;"
      % (10_000_000 * (mean_1y - euribor_12m_today)))
print("a fixed 1-year cash flow of 1,000,000 received in 2 years would be worth about %+.0f less when"
      " discounted at the expected rate instead of today's rate."
      % (1_000_000 * (1 / (1 + mean_1y) - 1 / (1 + euribor_12m_today))))
